source_read: PDF pp. 1691-1692 and the unnumbered third page (PDFs/MDMA/Mitchell_2021_ReplyToCritiques.pdf): text extraction and rendered p. 1691 for paragraph counts; MAPP1's Table 1 and competing-interests statement checked on its publisher page in my own tab. Step 1 not run this round.

design.note: Reply without data; editors' narrative-review checklist.

key_findings.note: Nine running-text paragraphs: eight starting on p. 1691, one on p. 1692.
MAPP1 Table 1 checked: no earlier therapy 2 (2.2%); CBT 34, EMDR 30, prolonged exposure 1.
Reference 5 is Jerome et al. (2020), Psychopharmacology 237, 2485-2497.

key_findings.correction: The quoted APA panel gives as its reason for not recommending psychotherapy before or instead of medicines, or using 'first-line', the lack of evidence from direct comparisons; the different stringency of the control conditions is offered as the implication (efficacy inferences may not be comparable across the two classes), not as the reason.

reporting_issues.note: MAPP1's competing interests: J.M.M. received funding from MAPS PBC during the conduct of the study, and J.M.M. and A.C. personal fees or grants from the Usona Institute.
'F. Naude' in the replying-to line; 'post-tramautic' in the 2nd paragraph; references 2 and 3 read 'Nat. Med. doi (2021)'.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: References 1, 4 and 5 are the authors' or the sponsor's, plus the maps.org pages for the special protocol assessment and the breakthrough designation.

domains.domain: Balance of evidence on the trial's comparator, blinding and durability

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial, with one correction to the claimed field: MAPP1's Table 1 can neither support nor refute that most participants had had first-line trauma-focused therapy, because CBT (34), EMDR (30) and prolonged exposure (1) are given without their overlap (between 34 and 65 of 90 had at least one) and CBT is not specified as trauma-focused; 'but not for first-line trauma-focused therapy' should read 'cannot be checked for first-line trauma-focused therapy'. The 13-word quotation is verbatim.

missed: The reply's statement that the cost-effectiveness of MDMA-assisted therapy had been evaluated on the phase 3 design and was under review (7th paragraph) is uncited; it bears on cl_mdma_ptsd_cost, whose critics' 2022 model (Marseille, Mitchell and Kahn) has the reply's first author's name among its authors.
The reply answers Burke and Blumberger only on blinding and only in principle; it does not give MAPP1's own anecdotal blinding figures (at least 10% wrong guesses), which were in the trial report.
